proofUses.reason: Pointwise first-step expansion and nonnegative Fourier transforms give the dimension-uniform small bound at a fixed parameter.
The unshifted bound retains the nearest-neighbour factor of order 1/d; Hölder controls all shifts in the supremum.
The Fourier identity retains the two connector masses. One Holder argument treats arbitrary pairs of shifts, completing all three cases.
The refined first coefficient is used at order one. Geometric summation gives absolute norms and moments before removing the remainder.
The certified sixth walk integral gives explicit unweighted and weighted integrals; retaining constants with bootstrap bound two gives five numerical diagram estimates.
Exact geometric sums retain the order-zero and refined order-one contributions, give a frequency budget of 50000000/d, and justify the full equation and absolute second moments.
